title: Cross-Border Scaling Under Pressure
description: Practice making high-stakes international expansion decisions involving unit economics, market sequencing, and scaling tradeoffs.

interactions.prompt: A B2B SaaS company expanding to DACH reports: CAC up 3.2x vs. US, LTV/CAC at 1.8, payback period 26 months, but net revenue retention is 135%. What's the critical signal?

options.text: CAC is too high; pause expansion immediately
135% NRR will compensate over time; optimize CAC on margins
26-month payback is acceptable for enterprise SaaS
LTV/CAC of 1.8 means the market is fundamentally unprofitable

chartData.title: DACH vs US Market Metrics Comparison

interactions.prompt: You're a marketplace (like Deliveroo) entering Southeast Asia. You can either launch in 5 cities simultaneously with thin ops teams, or deeply invest in Bangkok alone with full local infrastructure. Runway: 18 months.

options.text: 5 cities to capture network effects and data before competitors arrive
Bangkok only - prove unit economics, build repeatable playbook, then expand
Launch 2 cities with complementary demand profiles to test variance
Partner with a local incumbent to bypass operational setup entirely

interactions.prompt: When scaling internationally, the ratio of ____ to organic acquisition cost in each new market is the leading indicator of whether a localization investment will reach contribution margin positive.

options.text: Paid blended CAC
Brand awareness lift
Localized content conversion
Channel partner margin

interactions.prompt: A fintech (like Stripe) entering Latin America must sequence these activities. Rank by execution priority: (a) Hire country GM with regulatory expertise, (b) Obtain local payment licenses, (c) Sign 3 anchor merchants for demand validation, (d) Build local banking integrations.

options.text: Hire country GM with regulatory expertise
Obtain local payment licenses
Sign 3 anchor merchants for demand validation
Build local banking integrations

interactions.prompt: Your DTC brand expanded to Japan. Month 6 data: AOV 22% higher than US, repeat purchase rate 41% (vs 28% US), but ROAS on paid channels is 0.7x and organic search traffic is 85% lower than projected. What matters most?

options.text: Kill paid spend; the ROAS proves Japan won't work at scale
High AOV and repeat rates signal strong PMF; solve distribution, not demand
Focus on SEO optimization to close the organic traffic gap
Raise prices further since willingness-to-pay clearly exceeds US levels

chartData.title: Japan vs US Market Performance Comparison

interactions.prompt: Your PLG SaaS tool (like Notion) has 400K organic users in India but ARPU is $2/mo vs $14/mo globally. Engineering wants to build a localized free tier; finance wants to gate features to push upgrades. Board meeting is Friday.

options.text: Localized free tier - grow to dominance, monetize later via enterprise
Gate features - low ARPU markets must prove willingness to pay first
Tiered approach: free for individuals, paid for teams of 5+
Deprioritize India; reallocate resources to higher-ARPU European markets

interactions.prompt: A Series C healthtech scaling from US to UK, Germany, and UAE simultaneously must allocate a $12M expansion budget. Rank these by expected ROI efficiency: (a) Regulatory & compliance in all 3 markets, (b) Centralized multilingual product localization, (c) Country-specific sales teams with quota, (d) Regional brand campaign across all 3.

options.text: Regulatory & compliance in all 3 markets
Centralized multilingual product localization
Country-specific sales teams with quota
Regional brand campaign across all 3

interactions.prompt: Six months in, Germany's regulatory body delays your healthtech approval by 12+ months. UK is performing at 0.6x plan, but UAE hit 1.4x targets with unexpected B2G demand. You must reallocate 60% of Germany's remaining budget today.

options.text: Pour it all into UAE to maximize the B2G momentum
Split 70/30 UAE/UK - double down on winner, stabilize the underperformer
Split 50/50 UAE/UK to hedge against single-market concentration risk
Hold budget in reserve until Germany clears regulatory - preserve optionality

interactions.priorContext: Previously you planned equal budget allocation across US, UK, Germany, and UAE. Germany's regulatory delay fundamentally changes your expansion sequencing and forces rapid capital redeployment.
